From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Galileo — security audit packet shared; quick questions & next steps

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for carving out time earlier today. Quick recap and a couple asks so we can keep momentum with your security reviewers:

- Recap: we walked through Redwood's hosted API, Dedicated options, and our private deployment model (VPC). You flagged data residency and audit logging as primary evaluation points for Galileo's procurement team.
- What I attached: "redwood_security_audit_packet_v3.pdf" — includes SOC 2 scope, logging/retention defaults, encryption-at-rest details, key management options, and our incident response playbook.

A couple quick asks so we can prioritize:
1) Are there any specific sections your reviewers will need expanded (e.g., KMS integrations, HSM references, log schema)?
2) Who from your side will own the final sign-off on the security checklist (name + role)?
3) Do you have a target date for purchase decision or pilot kickoff? We can align availability for a 30-min deep-dive with our security eng if useful.

Possible next steps (feel free to pick one):
- 30-min technical Q&A with our security lead (Monica) — I'm proposing Thu 5/13 or Fri 5/14, midday ET.
- Written answers to any packet questions by EOD Fri if you send the list.
- A short live demo of the audit/logging configuration for your compliance engineer.

If it helps, I'll also mark the sections I think map to your checklist and send a one-pager.

Thanks — looking forward to hearing what the review process looks like on your side.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Connor: +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: redwood_security_audit_packet_v3.pdf (PDF, 1.4MB)

Following up on my note from last week — did the packet reach your reviewers? I know these queues can fill up fast. Two quick things I wanted to check:

- Priority: Is this review still on the same timeline you mentioned on our call, or has it shifted? If timing changed, we can adjust our availability.
- Blockers: Anything immediate that would prevent a quick Q&A (e.g., need for additional legal language, non-standard KMS requirements, or a compliance-only PoC)?

If it would be useful, Monica (cc'd) can join a short call to walk through the KMS/HSM section and the logging retention options — that usually clears up 80% of the questions we see. I'm available Fri 05/21 10:00am ET or Mon 05/24 2:00pm ET; otherwise tell me a time that works for your security lead and we'll make it work.

Quick note: we can also produce an extract that maps packet sections to your checklist items if you send that over — saves time for reviewers.

Thanks —
Connor

Thanks, Connor — and thanks for the packet. Apologies for the slow response; our security team dug into the PDF and surfaced two items they'd like to discuss before we move forward:

1) Key ownership model: we need clarity on customer-managed keys across Hosted API and Dedicated; our default requirement is customer KMS control for production data. The packet has options but the engineering notes were high-level.
2) Audit log retention & schema: our SOC reviewers asked whether we can extend retention for a pilot to 13 months and if you can provide the log schema for authentication events and admin actions.

Both look like conversation items rather than hard blockers. We'd prefer a short sync where your security engineer can walk through the KMS options and confirm feasibility for an extended retention window for the pilot.

Can we do Fri 05/21 at 10:00am ET? If that works I'll invite our security lead (Evan Park) and attach our internal checklist ahead of time.

Samira Khan
